# Let me try a different approach: a mixture of power laws
# P = w * P1 + (1-w) * P2 where P1 and P2 are power laws with different parameters

def mixture_power_law(w, alpha1, a1, alpha2, a2, n=vocab_size):
    indices = np.arange(n, dtype=np.float64) + 1
    
    P1_unnormalized = indices ** (-alpha1)
    P1 = P1_unnormalized / P1_unnormalized.sum()
    
    P2_unnormalized = (indices + a2 - 1) ** (-alpha2)
    P2 = P2_unnormalized / P2_unnormalized.sum()
    
    P = w * P1 + (1-w) * P2
    return P / P.sum()

def mixture_kl(params, n=vocab_size):
    w, alpha1, a1, alpha2, a2 = params
    if not (0 < w < 1 and alpha1 > 0 and alpha2 > 0 and a1 > 0 and a2 > 0):
        return 1e10, 1e10, None
    
    P = mixture_power_law(w, alpha1, a1, alpha2, a2, n)
    
    mask = P > 0
    kl_f = np.sum(P[mask] * np.log(P[mask] / U))
    kl_b = np.sum(U * np.log(U / P))
    
    return kl_f, kl_b, P
